description:
## Goal

Write `test/filament/examples/collaboration_test.exs` — tests for the Collaboration
example from G4.

Tests use Rung 3 (real `Collaboration.DocumentServer`) and direct server API calls.
Key scenarios:
- Lock acquire succeeds for first requester
- Lock acquire rejected for second requester while first holds it
- Lock released when holder process dies (`:DOWN` on the server)
- Presence count tracks number of active subscribers
- DocumentEditor component renders "Locked" or "Edit" based on observable view

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await
guidance. Do not improvise.

---

## 0. Prerequisites — read implementations first

Before writing any test code, read:

  - `examples/collaboration/lib/collaboration/document_server.ex`
    — ALL of it, especially:
      (a) The state struct and how lock_holder/presence are tracked
      (b) `acquire_lock/2` and `release_lock/2` public API signatures
      (c) `handle_subscribe/3` — what it returns as the observable view
      (d) `handle_unsubscribe/2` — does it exist? (Track D may or may not inject this)
      (e) `observable_view/1` private function — what fields are in the view?
          Confirmed from G4 spec: %{locked: boolean, lock_holder: pid|nil, presence: integer}
      (f) Whether the server also implements Hold manually or uses a separate API

  - `examples/collaboration/lib/collaboration_web/components/document_editor.ex`
    — What props it takes (:server, :doc_id or similar)
    — What it renders when locked vs available

  - The Filament.Test API (mount/3, update/1, eventually/2) from Track F

  - CRITICAL: G4's implementation note — DocumentServer uses ONLY
    `use Filament.Observable.GenServer` (NOT `use Filament.Hold.GenServer`).
    Lock management is implemented manually to avoid a duplicate :DOWN handler
    compiler error. This means locking is done via custom GenServer calls
    (acquire_lock/release_lock), not via Filament.Hold.acquire/release.
    If the actual implementation differs, adapt accordingly and comment.

---

## 1. Test file location

FILE: `test/filament/examples/collaboration_test.exs`

`examples/collaboration/lib/` is already in `elixirc_paths(:test)` from G4.

---

## 2. Tests

```elixir
defmodule Filament.Examples.CollaborationTest do
  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
  import Filament.Test

  # Helpers to subscribe manually to Document.Server's observable stream
  # (for testing observable notifications without a full component mount)

  defp manual_subscribe(server, fiber_id) do
    sub = %Filament.Observable.Subscriber{
      pid: self(),
      fiber_id: fiber_id,
      slot_index: 0,
      project: &Function.identity/1
    }
    Filament.Observable.subscribe(server, nil, sub)
  end

  # ── Server-level tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe "Collaboration.DocumentServer" do
    setup do
      {:ok, server} = Collaboration.DocumentServer.start_link(doc_id: "test-doc")
      %{server: server}
    end

    test "lock acquired by first requester", %{server: server} do
      # acquire_lock/2 signature: acquire_lock(server, requester_pid)
      # Returns {:ok} or {:error, :locked} — adapt to actual return shape
      result = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())
      assert result == :ok or match?({:ok, _}, result)
    end

    test "lock rejected when already held", %{server: server} do
      :ok = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())

      # Second requester (different pid) gets :locked
      parent = self()
      spawn(fn ->
        result = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())
        send(parent, {:lock_result, result})
      end)
      assert_receive {:lock_result, {:error, :locked}}, 1000
    end

    test "lock released on holder process death", %{server: server} do
      parent = self()

      holder = spawn(fn ->
        :ok = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())
        send(parent, :acquired)
        receive do: (:stop -> :ok)
      end)

      assert_receive :acquired, 1000

      # Kill the holder — DocumentServer's :DOWN handler should release the lock
      # (DocumentServer uses Observable.GenServer which injects :DOWN handling;
      # G4 also manually monitors the lock holder — confirm in implementation)
      Process.exit(holder, :kill)
      Process.sleep(50)

      # Now we should be able to acquire
      result = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())
      assert result == :ok or match?({:ok, _}, result)
    end

    test "release_lock/2 frees the lock", %{server: server} do
      :ok = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())
      :ok = Collaboration.DocumentServer.release_lock(server, self())

      # Should be acquirable again
      result = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())
      assert result == :ok or match?({:ok, _}, result)
    end

    test "presence count reflects subscriber count via observable notifications", %{server: server} do
      # Subscribe manually. handle_subscribe should increment presence and notify observers.
      {:ok, view1} = manual_subscribe(server, :presence_test_1)
      # view1 is the initial observable view returned from handle_subscribe
      # Confirm it has presence=1
      assert is_map(view1) and Map.get(view1, :presence) == 1

      # Subscribe again (same test process, different fiber_id)
      {:ok, view2} = manual_subscribe(server, :presence_test_2)
      # The first subscriber should receive a presence=2 notification
      assert_receive {:filament_observable_update, :presence_test_1, 0, %{presence: 2}}, 500
      # view2's initial value should also reflect presence=2 (since handle_subscribe
      # increments before returning the initial value)
      assert Map.get(view2, :presence) == 2
    end
  end

  # ── Rung-3 component tests ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

  describe "DocumentEditor component (rung-3)" do
    setup do
      {:ok, server} = Collaboration.DocumentServer.start_link(doc_id: "edit-test")
      {:ok, view} = mount(
        CollaborationWeb.Components.DocumentEditor,
        %{server: server}
      )
      %{server: server, view: view}
    end

    test "renders 'Edit' button when document is not locked", %{view: view} do
      # DocumentEditor should show an "Edit" or "Lock and Edit" button
      # when no one has the lock. Adapt to actual rendered text.
      text = render_text(view)
      assert text =~ "Edit" or text =~ "edit" or text =~ "Lock"
      refute text =~ "Locked by"
    end

    test "renders 'Locked' when another user holds the lock", %{server: server, view: view} do
      # Acquire the lock from a different pid
      parent = self()
      other_holder = spawn(fn ->
        :ok = Collaboration.DocumentServer.acquire_lock(server, self())
        send(parent, :locked)
        receive do: (:stop -> :ok)
      end)

      assert_receive :locked, 1000

      # view is subscribed; drain observable updates to re-render
      view = Filament.Test.update(view)

      text = render_text(view)
      assert text =~ "Locked" or text =~ "locked" or text =~ "unavailable"

      # Clean up
      Process.exit(other_holder, :kill)
    end

    test "presence indicator updates when second client mounts", %{server: server, view: view} do
      # view is already subscribed (presence=1 from handle_subscribe in mount)
      initial_text = render_text(view)
      assert initial_text =~ "1"  # "1 online" or similar; adapt to actual rendering

      # Second client subscribes to the same server (from a different process).
      # This is tricky in single-process tests because both views would share the
      # same owner_pid mailbox. Simulate by manually subscribing.
      {:ok, _initial_view2} = manual_subscribe(server, :presence_viewer_2)

      # view should now receive {:filament_observable_update, ...} with presence=2
      view = Filament.Test.update(view)
      text = render_text(view)
      assert text =~ "2"  # "2 online" or presence indicator; adapt to actual rendering
    end
  end
end
```

NOTE on `manual_subscribe/2` in component tests: The `describe "DocumentEditor"` block
uses `manual_subscribe/2` to simulate a second subscriber without mounting a second
component in the same process (which would cause mailbox confusion). If the DocumentServer
doesn't expose the `Filament.Observable.subscribe/3` API directly, adapt to use
`GenServer.call(server, {:filament_subscribe, nil, sub})` which is the raw message
injected by `use Filament.Observable.GenServer`. Check Track D's macro expansion for
the exact subscribe message format.

---

## 3. Run tests

```
mix test test/filament/examples/collaboration_test.exs
```

---

## 4. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `test/filament/examples/collaboration_test.exs` exists and compiles
- [ ] All 4 DocumentServer tests pass (acquire, rejected, death-release, release, presence)
- [ ] All 3 DocumentEditor component tests pass (unlocked, locked, presence indicator)
- [ ] `async: true` — each test creates its own server
- [ ] No changes to example source files
- [ ] Full suite still passes: `mix test`
